reviews.text: I turned to this clinic after noticing that my 9-year-old Golden Retriever Bice was starting to limp after a few meters during walks. X-rays revealed hip dysplasia, and we began physical therapy with Dr. Ilaria Terruzzi. Through laser therapy and water treadmill sessions, Bice is back to running happily. I thank Ilaria for her incredible empathy and professionalism; I've never met a better vet!

I had a terrible experience with my dog. The nurse was kind, but the doctor was a bit self-important. He didn't examine animals properly, but did it in a general way just to get a bill. Not recommended.
Terrible experience, zero empathy for the animal. They're just trying to sell useless therapies without a diagnosis.

Terrible experience. Dr. Mangiagalli misdiagnosed my dog ​​and for months refused to perform any tests after a car accident. After two months, he decided to do some tests, X-rays, and postural tests to check his paws, because I'd been telling him for months that he wasn't running well and wasn't placing his paws properly. After the tests, the doctor agreed with me, but instead of looking for a cure or a rehabilitation program, he told me he didn't know what to do and that the only solution was to take his swimming lessons, which he tries to push on all his patients.
In short, the doctor was too full of himself, lacked empathy, and was unprofessional, given that after a car accident, he didn't even perform a test, only touched them with his magical hands that diagnose everything by touch.
I changed vets, had MRIs, and other tests, and the source of the problem was found. We're now undergoing treatment, and the dog is doing much better. I was informed that if this process had been started sooner, it would have taken less time and the dog would have suffered much less.
I've already spoken to my lawyer, since luckily I recorded all the hearings in which he told me that the dog was fine even if it wasn't true.
It solved a good part of the problem for my dog.... reasonable prices.

Dr. Mangiagalli is fantastic, humane, and helpful! His entire staff is also always courteous and kind.

We also have a little mixed-breed dog, almost 15 years old, who, thanks to him, despite her numerous problems, is still with us and living a dignified life. Top 100, trust me!

I've been taking my dog ​​to the European Veterinary Clinic for 2 years, and I wouldn't trade it for any other. Dr. Gerard Mangiagalli, always kind and helpful, and his wonderful support staff are always ready to guide you and advise you on the right things to do with your four-legged friend.
It's the best clinic in Lombardy. I've always been happy there and I won't change. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND IT AS A CLINIC. WARMEST REGARDS TO DR. MANGIAGALLI AND ALL THE STAFF. IF YOU WANT STAFF READY TO CARE FOR YOUR FURRY, BRING THEM TO THEM.

Attracted by the positive reviews, I brought my guinea pig here to have it examined by Dr. Mangiagalli. He prescribed a treatment that didn't work, but the problem is that I was never able to contact him again to understand what to do with the guinea pig. The secretary always answered me saying she would call me back. At that point, obviously, I went to another vet who is an expert in exotics and who performed a much more thorough and detailed examination. The thing that disappoints me is that if Dr. Mangiagalli wasn't an expert in exotics, he should have been honest and said so rather than performing such a superficial examination. In the end, it's always our pet who loses out, and I find it unfair and incorrect, especially not to have a second opinion after a visit that was carried out and for which money was spent.

A negative and painful experience!!
We went to the European Veterinary Clinic to see Dr. Mangiagalli with our dog, Mia, a 13-year-old Gordon Setter, because we thought she had age-related arthritis.
She was then subjected to physiotherapy and other treatments for that condition.
Unfortunately, however, Mia had something else entirely, and it wasn't clear, despite the fact that the clinical exams and ultrasound suggested further investigation rather than rehabilitative exercises and PRP, which were both unnecessary and expensive.
Within a few weeks, Mia's condition worsened, and at that point we stopped the physiotherapy and performed further tests that indicated Cushing's disease as the cause of her problems. However, because she was so weak, she couldn't begin treatment, so she was admitted to the day hospital for antibiotics and anti-inflammatory therapy.
After four days in the outpatient clinic and one day at home (Sunday), Mia's condition worsened, and we rushed her to another clinic, where they immediately told us her condition was critical, as her liver (that was her problem) had stopped functioning.
After two days in intensive care, we had to "put her to sleep" and say goodbye, heartbroken, to avoid further suffering, asking for forgiveness for not having protected her enough.
What we found, unfortunately, was superficiality and a lack of listening; always trust your instincts, don't settle for just one explanation or one opinion, because the lives of our animals depend on us.
Nicola Cellamare
